sources.title: Import Subscribers
sources.content:
Quickly import your email subscribers from another platform.
This guide will show you how to import a CSV file of your subscribers so that they'll be notified each time you publish a post on your site.
Add up to 100 subscribers
People with a free Jetpack plan may import up to 100 subscribers. This counts both towards a bulk .csv import or adding subscribers manually one at a time. The 100-subscriber limit on the free plan is a total cap on your account, not a per-import limit.
Add up to 10,000 subscribers
If you upgrade your plan to Growth, Social, Security, or Complete, or if you have our legacy Jetpack Creator plan, you can import up to 10,000 subscribers.
To help protect against spam, the free plan limits importing up to 100 subscribers. Paid plans have no limit, but imports of more than 10,000 subscribers will go through a manual review.
No matter what plan you have, there is no limit to the number of people who can choose to subscribe to your blog directly via your subscription form or the WordPress.com Reader.
Writing engaging content and promoting it via Jetpack Blaze or to your social media is a great way to have more followers.
Before you import
Get permission
Please ensure that you have permission to email your subscribers. If we receive complaints from your subscribers about spam, or if your emails have a high bounce rate, we may take action against your account.
Clean up your list
Subscriber list hygiene is important for successful imports. If our tools suspect that too many of your email addresses are invalid, your import may fail.
Do your best to have a clean and updated list when importing your subscribers to Jetpack. When you have an old list or if you haven't sent any emails to your subscribers in more than 1 year, it is very likely that over 10% of the email addresses no longer exist because people change jobs.
To prevent this from happening, we strongly suggest that you clean your subscribers' lists using a third-party service, such as the ones listed below:
Kickbox (free up to 100 addresses)
Emailable (free up to 250 addresses)
Proofy
EmailListVerify
NeverBounce
Klemail (France)
emailvalidation.io (free up to 100 addresses)
Import your subscriber list
To import subscribers, follow these steps:
Head to your Subscription dashboard at https://cloud.jetpack.com/subscribers/yourjetpack.blog (replace yourjetpack.blog with your site's domain).
Click the Add Subscribers button at the top right end of the screen.
If you have just a few email addresses to add, you can type them in the boxes provided. Alternatively, click the uploading a CSV file link to select a file from your computer.
Click the Add subscribers button after you have made your selection.
You can either manually type in email addresses, or upload a CSV file that you downloaded from another email platform. When uploading a CSV file, all email addresses in your CSV file will be imported.
Import from Substack
You can import free and paid subscribers from Substack, along with your entire Newsletter if you'd like. Head to your Subscription dashboard at https://cloud.jetpack.com/subscribers/yourjetpack.blog (replace yourjetpack.blog with your site's domain). Click on Import from Substack, and follow the instructions.
Import subscribers with Newsletter categories
You can import subscribers directly into specific Newsletter categories, both manually and via CSV uploads, via the Jetpack Cloud dashboard.
The feature is available on Jetpack Cloud → Subscribers when the Newsletter module, Newsletter categories, and categories are all enabled and selected in Jetpack → Settings → Newsletter. You can read more about that on the Newsletter Categories documentation page.
Manage your subscribers
You can view your imported subscribers from your dashboard by clicking on Users and then clicking on the Subscribers tab.
Here, you can:
Click Add Subscribers to add more subscribers.
Remove individual subscribers.
Note: At this time, there is no way to manually change a subscriber’s status from free to paid. If you are importing subscribers and some of them should be marked as paid, try re-importing only your paid subscribers. This may update their subscription details correctly.
Publish a Post
When you publish a post, an email is sent to all your email subscribers. When you click Publish on a new post, scroll down until you see the number of subscribers to which the post will be sent.
Jetpack will only send out notifications for new public posts. Publishing other content types (like pages or a custom post type) or updating an already published post will not send a notification email.
Migrate subscribers from a WordPress.com site
If you want to migrate subscribers from a WordPress.com website to a self-hosted Jetpack-connected site, you can use our Subscription migration tool.
Troubleshoot issues with subscribers import
Errors during import
If you face any errors importing a CSV file of followers, here are a few things to verify first:
Go through your subscriber email list and make sure that all of the email addresses are valid. If we detect any invalid email addresses, the import will not work.
Make sure you have collected all your subscriber email addresses by yourself and that you have not purchased any subscriber lists. We take spam very seriously, and your email list will be blocked if we detect known spam addresses.
If you have lots of email addresses, try importing them in smaller batches of 500 each (this only applies if you have Growth, Social, Security, Complete, or the legacy Jetpack Creator plan).
Here is a list of common subscriber import errors, and what you can do about them:
Error Message  Explanation Suggested Action     Can't start subscriber import while another one is running. Another import is already running. Make sure you haven't started imports in another tab. Otherwise, contact support.   No subscribers have been submitted. An empty file was submitted. Examine your CSV file and double-check whether it's empty.   The CSV file does not contain information. The CSV file is empty. Examine your CSV file and double-check whether it's empty.   You cannot add more subscribers on the free plan. It is only possible to import up to 100 subscribers without a paid Jetpack Creator, Jetpack Social plan or bundled Jetpack plan. There is a limit of 100 subscribers on the free plan. Please upgrade to one of those: Jetpack Social, Jetpack Growth, Jetpack Security, Jetpack Complete.   You are not allowed to manage subscribers for the specified site. The user account does not have permission to manage users on the site (likely because the account has a different role). Try performing the action from an administrator account.   Your recent import is taking longer than expected to complete. -  Contact support.   Any other error -  Contact support.
Subscribers not imported
If you receive an email saying that not all of your subscribers have been imported, here's why:
Some email domains are known spammers or abusers, so we block such domains from receiving email.
The email address you tried to add is associated with a WordPress.com user account that has chosen not to receive email.
The email address has too many pending invites for subscriptions.
Export subscribers to a different platform
You can export your subscribers list as a CSV file. You can follow the steps on this page to do that.
Still need help?
Please contact support. We're happy to advise.

sources.title: Hire An Expert
sources.content:
Let us help bring 
your vision to life
Elevate your online presence with our hand-picked network of exceptional WordPress agencies ready to bring your vision to life. With our expert matching process, we simplify and expedite your search for the perfect agency, ensuring a seamless experience from conception to launch.
Match me with an agency
What to expect
You can expect to be matched with an agency in three business days or less. The duration of your project may vary, depending on the complexity and your desired timeline.
1. Share your vision
The more you tell us, the better we can match you with an agency that’s tailored to your specific needs. From design preferences to desired functionality, every nuance helps craft a more precise proposal and keeps the project aligned with your expectations. Projects start at $5,000.
If you’re budget is lower, check out our Partner Directory for agencies that can fit your budget.
2. Connect with an agency
We’ll connect you with the WordPress experts best suited to your project. They will set up a discovery call where you can dive deeper and ensure every aspect of your website vision is captured.
3. Receive your proposal
Get a unique proposal for your project, with detailed pricing and next steps outlined. Turn your project vision into a reality and gear up for launch!
Match me with an agency
Why trust us to find your perfect WordPress agency?
Precision matching
We understand your project needs and connect you with agencies that align perfectly with your vision  
and requirements.
Save time
Skip the lengthy vetting process. Our extensive network helps you find the right agency faster.
Vetted expertise
Our agencies are WordPress specialists with proven track records in design  
and development.
Quality focus
We partner only with  agencies that consistently deliver excellence and meet  high standards.
Match me with an agency
Match me with an agency
To help us match you with the best agency for your needs, please fill out the form with as much detail  
as possible.
By submitting this form, you consent to sharing your contact details and project information with prospective agencies.
Frequently asked questions
Can I be matched with an agency if I have a smaller project?
We offer introductions to agency partners if your project has a budget of $5k or more. These agency partners can help transform your vision into a dynamic online presence that aligns with your goals and brand identity.
If you’re working with a smaller budget, we recommend exploring our agency partner directory. Here, you can connect with an agency of your choosing. Our expert partners are available and ready to assist clients of all project sizes.
How does it work?
Please fill out the form to the best of your ability. The more information we have about your project, the faster we can match you to an agency partner. From there, we’ll match you with an agency who will guide you through a step-by-step process to understand your vision and bring it to life by designing and building your custom website.
Where is my website hosted?
For custom sites, our agency partners will comprehensively assess your site’s requirements and propose the most suitable hosting options tailored to your business needs.
Do I own my website after the work is completed?
Yes, the website is yours once it’s finished. You’ll be able to add and edit copy, images, and more, directly from the WordPress Admin Dashboard.
Do you offer a maintenance package?
When you opt for a custom development approach for your website, you unlock the opportunity to purchase additional, comprehensive maintenance plans from our agency partners. 
Maintenance packages are tailored to support your evolving needs—covering everything from expanded functionality with additional pages to regular code updates, as well as plugin configurations, and more. If you’re interested in ongoing maintenance, please be sure to mention this in your form submission and subsequent conversions with the agency partner we match you with.
Can I use my existing domain name?
Yes, our agency partners will help you connect your existing domain name to your site after the build is complete.

sources.title: Export a WordPress.com site to WordPress.org
sources.content:
Moving your website from WordPress.com to WordPress.org may seem intimidating, but it's a manageable process. You can continue enjoying the benefits of Jetpack on any hosting platform. 
Keep the features you like with the Jetpack plugin
The transition from WordPress.com doesn't mean you'll lose the powerful tools Jetpack provides for security, performance, and site management. Keep the value of Jetpack in mind as you take your website to its new home. When you migrate, you can also transfer your subscribers and stats.
You can follow the steps listed below to start the site migration from WordPress.com to WordPress.org.
Migrate the site content
You can use WordPress's built-in export/import tools to transfer your content (posts, pages, media, etc.) from WordPress.com to WordPress.org.
Export your site from WordPress.com by navigating to the Tools → Export page in your dashboard
From there, download all of your content in a single file, as per the instructions on this page.
Now that your content is exported, the importing process will happen on a third-party hosting provider. However, our support services do not cover this. However, you can refer to the following resources that might assist you in navigating the import procedure on your new platform:
WordPress Import – for import-related documentation.
Migrating a WordPress Site – for a comprehensive migration guide.
Tools - Import and Export Tutorial – for a learning resource with hands-on tutorials.
We encourage you to contact your hosting provider for personalized assistance throughout the import process.
Migrating Subscribers and Stats
To migrate your email and WordPress.com subscribers, you must install and activate the Jetpack plugin on your new WordPress.org site.
Once activated, Jetpack offers a migration tool to transfer your followers (email and WordPress.com subscribers) from your WordPress.com site.
Jetpack can also transfer your site stats. Once it is installed on your WordPress.org site and connected to your WordPress.com account, your stats should display. If they don't, contact support.
Get started with Jetpack
Once your site has been successfully exported to a WordPress.org installation and Jetpack is activated and well-connected, you're ready to start enjoying the features you loved when your site was hosted on WordPress.com.
Please check out Getting Started with Jetpack Guide to feel more accustomed to Jetpack on WordPress.org.
If you have an existing Jetpack plan to transfer, or you need to transfer your Jetpack connection to a different user, you can check this guide instead.
Still need help?
Please contact support. We're happy to advise.

sources.title: Transfer your Jetpack connection or plan to another user
sources.content:
You can transfer ownership of your Jetpack connection and/or your Jetpack plan to any other connected admin user on your site.
Site owners are users who have connected Jetpack to WordPress.com.
Plan purchasers are users who purchased a paid plan for the site.
Generally, it is best if these are the same person. It is possible, though, for them to differ. For example, a developer may be the site owner, because they set up the website and connected Jetpack to WordPress.com, and their client may be the plan purchaser, who used their connected WordPress.com account and billing information to purchase the plan for the site.
Before you begin, be sure to add a new WP Admin Administrator-level user (see guide) and have them connect their account to Jetpack with their WordPress.com account.
Change the site owner
Note that transferring the site's ownership does not transfer the plans active on the site to the new user. If you have active plans that you want to transfer, check also our Change the plan purchaser guide. Before starting the process, double-check if you wish to transfer the site connection ownership, the plans, or both.
To change the site owner for your site:
From your site's WP Admin dashboard, navigate to Jetpack → My Jetpack.
Scroll to the bottom of the page and find the Connection area.
Click Manage or Site and account connected.
Click Transfer ownership to another admin.
Under "Site Ownership," you'll find the current site owner.
Choose new owner: In the Site owner drop-down list, select the user you want to transfer ownership to. If the new user does not show in the dropdown, ensure that the new user:
Has an administrator account on your site.
Has connected their administrator account to their WordPress.com account.
Select a user to become the new Site owner and click the Transfer ownership button to complete the transfer.
Once the transfer is complete, note that you won't be able to revert the changes. Only the new owner will have the authority to make further adjustments.
Under the Site owner in the Site ownership section, you will see this notice: "Somebody else owns this site's connection to WordPress.com."
Change the plan purchaser
If you need to transfer the plan to another user, the steps depend on the type of plan you have.
For Jetpack bundles (Complete, Security, Growth) and legacy plans (Jetpack Personal, Jetpack Premium, Jetpack Professional), you can transfer the plan yourself directly from WP Admin.
For all other plans, the transfer requires help from our support team. Make sure the new user has an Administrator account connected to WordPress.com, then contact support directly and provide their email address.
Plans listed below require that you contact us and request the transfer:
Jetpack Akismet Anti-Spam
Jetpack AI Assistant
Jetpack Boost
Jetpack Scan
Jetpack Search
Jetpack Social
Jetpack Stats
Jetpack VaultPress Backup
Jetpack VideoPress
CRM Entrepreneur
Alternatively, you can also consider to cancel and refund the plan, and re-purchase it by using the correct WordPress.com/ Jetpack account.
Transfer a plan yourself (only available for Jetpack bundles and legacy plans)
Here is how to transfer a Jetpack bundle (Complete, Security, and Growth) or a legacy plan (Jetpack Personal, Jetpack Premium, and Jetpack Professional):
From your site's WP Admin dashboard, navigate to Jetpack → My Jetpack.
Scroll to the bottom of the page and find the Connection area.
Click Manage or Site and account connected.
Click Transfer ownership to another admin.
Under "Site Ownership," you'll find the current plan purchaser.
Choose new plan purchaser: In the Plan purchaser drop-down list, select the user you want to transfer the bundle or the legacy plan to.  
If the Plan   Purchaser dropdown does not appear, ensure that the plan you want to transfer is one of the following: Jetpack Complete, Jetpack Security, Jetpack Growth, Jetpack Personal, Jetpack Premium, or Jetpack Professional. For other plans, contact our support directly. 
If the new user does not show in the dropdown, ensure that the new user:
Has an administrator account on your site.
Has connected their administrator account to their WordPress.com account.
Select a user to become the new Plan purchaser and confirm by clicking Yes, change the plan purchaser.
Once the transfer is complete, note that you won't be able to revert the changes. Only the new plan purchaser will have the authority to make further adjustments.
Under the Plan purchaser in the Site ownership section, you will see this notice: "Somebody else is the plan purchaser for this site."
If you change the Plan purchaser, the new Plan purchaser will need to add payment details in order to enable automatic renewal of the plan. They will receive an email prompting them to add new payment details.
Determine the owner of the plan
All plans that you purchased or that were transferred to your account appear at https://wordpress.com/me/purchases.
If you need to determine which account owns a plan active on your site but that does not appear at https://wordpress.com/me/purchases, please contact our support team   directly. If possible, share the transaction ID for the charge associated with this subscription.
Export a site to WordPress.org
If you need to transfer a site from WordPress.com to WordPress.org, you can follow the instructions on this page.
Still need help?
Please contact support. We're happy to advise.

sources.title: Move your Jetpack Plan to a Different Site/URL
sources.content:
Jetpack plans (such as Jetpack Security, Growth, or Complete) can only be used on one site at a time. If you need to switch your plan to a different site, there are a few ways to do it, depending on your situation:
1. Your Plan Is About to Renew
If your plan is close to its renewal date and you're moving to a new site:
Step 1: Cancel your current plan before it renews.
Step 2: Purchase a new Jetpack plan for the new site.
Cancel your plan →
2. You’re Within the Refund Period
Jetpack plans are eligible for a refund if you're within these timeframes:
Yearly plans: Refundable within 14 days of purchase.
Monthly plans: Refundable within 7 days of purchase.
If you're still within the refund period:
Step 1: Cancel and request a refund.
Step 2: Buy the same plan for your new site.
Request a refund →
3. You Need to Move the Plan (and You're Outside the Refund Window)
If you’re not eligible for a refund, we can transfer the plan for you.
What to do:
Connect Jetpack on the new site using the same WordPress.com account. 
→ Choose Jetpack Free during setup.
If you're using Jetpack Backup, download your latest backup before the transfer. 
→ After the move, backups from the original site will no longer be available.
Contact Jetpack Support and provide:
The current site URL where the plan is active
The new site URL where you'd like it moved
Contact Support →
Notes
A Jetpack plan can only be used on one site at a time.
Transferring a plan does not transfer backups or historical data.
The plan must be managed under the same WordPress.com account on both sites.
Still need help?
Please contact support. We're happy to advise.
